text:
When you open the communications channel, you hear faint voices of soldiers reporting to their superior, and when the image comes into focus, you see a woman wearing the epaulettes of an Admiral.

"The fact of the matter is," explains the slightly graying female Admiral $personName:"The previous mission target has been eliminated for unknown reasons, and the task we currently have on hand is a military procurement project of substantial size — deliver to me, by any means necessary, three mothballed Yoshura-class starships. What do you say?"

You carefully consider this unusual mission...

"Changed your mind?"

The female Admiral showed no trace of urgency, and seemed extraordinarily patient about the matter.

"Excellent, I await your good news."

A hint of relief flashed across the female Admiral's face as she cut the comms.
"Done already?" Over the comms, the female Admiral looks at you with surprise in her eyes.

text:
"Let us meet dockside." You nod as the female Admiral cuts the comm link.

You alight at the docks, and after a quick security check, meet the female Admiral face to face.

"Well done." Says the middle aged Admiral, as she gave your shoulder an approving pat.

"See that battlecruiser over there? In half a month, that old thing will be transferred to Enigma 3 for dismantling. Care to take a closer look?"

You ascend to the open side decks, where rows of gun turrets are arranged in a rectangular formations along the central axis... This appears to be a modified Yoshura, and judging by her rather distinctive livery, you realize that you've never seen a warship like this in the docks before... You notice a palm-sized holoprojector sitting on a long table in the command room, out of place among surroundings dim from the lack of power, the device still projecting a bust of a man.

"Less a vessel of glory, more a crystallized memory."

The Admiral walking in front of you mumbles inexplicably before turning around abruptly, her right prosthetic eye locking onto yours.

"The mission you completed was merely a test, but before we proceed to the main affair, let's talk about something else."

---- After navigating through dark, narrow maintenance ducts, you emerge with the Admiral from the starboard airlock, Port A. ----

The glare of the midday sun makes you squint, as a shrill voice rings in your ears: "All of Enigma bore witness to our love... and neither of us was prepared for separation, but the Gender Revolution had reached a tipping point." The Admiral suddenly chokes up a little, and draws out her next words, "---He was always such a quiet man. Who could've predicted that he would be the one to mobilize the Orbital Dockyard workers and lower ranked Sailors, bringing instability to the fringes of the system?"

"At that time, there was an ongoing war, a full-scale conflict against the Hegemony. From the beginning, beyond general mobilization, the hawks of war were already sharpening their claws... The two fleets crept slowly like colossal beasts along the fringes of a meteorite-strewn star system, inching toward each other over days while cautiously pointing their most offensive fronts at each other. Fleet maneuvers on such scales are a spectacle in this sector. Sub-fleets and scouting groups extended as far as three light-years out. On the first day, engagement went smoothly, with battles fought on four fronts, and the Hegemony's vanguard suffering heavy losses, and reducing one of their battleships to little more than scrap.

On the second day, mutiny struck. He led mutineers in an axial jump, quickly disengaging from the battlefield and firing off a surge to jam communications before high command could react. The situation deteriorated rapidly, and the right flank collapsed. We escaped only at grievous cost, leaving the glory of the Valkyries behind, along with fleet superiority. As one of the three commanders of the right flank, I was impeached, and although I was not convicted of the charges, I have been under house arrest ever since, and as you can see, although I can still express my political views, my voice is not heard."
options: 0:vft_continue:You can't help but lean forward, anticipating further development

text:
"After the battle, the 'traitors' did little more than leave the system... But the Valkyrie never gave up hunting them down." The female Admiral paused, her expression unreadable, before continuing:

"In truth, a report of suspected fleet signatures in a certain system's near-orbit remained on my personal computer even after I retired... That's where he's hiding, and if high command knows, treason and the gallows will be his fate.

This must end, but I didn't want him to die in shame... That's why I looked for you! You — the only captain with the patience and skill to handle this quietly... and when it's done, the spoils are all yours."

"What... do you think? " The female Admiral's voice was shaky, and a little distant.

text:
Unexpectedly, you receive a comms request, and when you answer, you are surprised to find the man talking to himself, as if he understood why you had come.

"You're the one she sent, aren't you? This day has come not a moment too soon."

The leader of the wanderers looks at you through drooping eyelids, looking a bit downtrodden, and more like a roadside beggar than a Fleet Admiral.

"Years of journeying through the void have taken their toll on a ship that used to carry the hopes and passions of the revolutionaries. We tried building our own utopia, only to lose all our fuel money in the New World. The damned Alliance merchants manipulated the fragile colonial economy, creating famine and squeezing every last credit from the hands of the people."

"By the time I realized that destroying the merchantile fleet would make it impossible for us to gain a foothold in Alliance worlds, it was too late. The fleet sailed outward, always outward. From the long outer channel of the Atlantean Nebula to lawless sanctuaries and through creepy fringe systems, we've been through fighting, infighting, betrayals and farewells again and again, right up to this very moment.

Yet she still carries that grudge? You seem to know something about the dark side of the Valkyries, and I wouldn't mind telling you more before we fight."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"Didn't both of you once loved each other? How did it come to this?"

text: "At some point, communication stalled, and both sides quietly asserted their own justice through actions... And on the eve of the great battle, my followers and I stowed old-style carbines and electromagnetic rifles in supply crates, and smuggling them aboard the battleship. We couldn't afford to let this opportunity slip, while the terrifying weight of interstellar tyranny was suffocating our movement, to escape the Valkyrie's sphere of influence! It was our only way out..."
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"There is no denying that it was a great struggle."

text:
"We steeled our resolve as we seized control of a sub-fleet. The revolutionaries boarded the Yoshura prototype undetected and killed the guards, whose impulse deflector fields collapsed under concentrated fire. The fall of this battleship was our movement's greatest triumph."

"The outpost was our final target, and after our armed forces ransacked it, we broke away from the organization and became denizens of the silent void. With the bones of the captured battleship, and the secrets we found in the outpost, I built this war machine, and decided to defend my life's purpose to the end with iron and with blood!"

His eyes burned with unyielding conviction as he raised his right hand to cut off the comm link.
options: 0:vft_he_continue:"If I may ask one last question, what do you think of her now?"

text: "To me, she was, and always will be, the only one for me." Silence engulfed both sides. For a moment, he looks at you, the stars in his eyes seemingly eternal, before resolutely disconnecting the comm link and ending his message abruptly, signaling the end of a story and the coming of a battle.
"I loath her." The comms fall silent as the flagship shakes violently. You look over the bridge, where someone is shouting "We are under attack! We are under attack!"
"From the moment we abandoned the organization, we had nothing more to do with each other." There comes a buzz, and the comms falls dead.
